subject: Deferred ramp payment plan & exception request - CloudBridge 3yr
messages:
From: Paul Gray <paul.gray@cloudbridge.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Li <anna.li@cloudbridge.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Payment cadence for multi-year commitment

Rachel —

Thanks for the demo last week. CloudBridge is excited about the 3‑year commitment option you outlined; the product fits an important part of our roadmap. Finance is pushing back on a full upfront prepay and wants a more distributed payment cadence. Two asks from our side: a) can Redwood accept a partial upfront (25% at signing) with the remainder split over year 1 & 2 as a ramp, and b) can we get Net 90 on milestone invoices for the first 12 months?

We understand discounts are tied to prepay — hoping we can get a structure that preserves a term discount while giving our treasury breathing room. attaching a short note from our accounting team for context.

— Paul
Paul Gray
Head of Platforms, CloudBridge
paul.gray@cloudbridge.com
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Paul Gray <paul.gray@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Payment cadence for multi-year commitment

Paul — thanks for the note and the accounting context. We can be flexible; below is a proposal that balances your treasury constraints with our pricing model. I attached a one‑page payment schedule (RBW‑3241_proposed_payment_schedule.xlsx) and the updated SOW showing deliverable milestones.

Proposal (high level):
- Commitment: 3 years, committed ARR basis
- Upfront: 25% at signing (applies as a prepay credit)
- Ramp: 40% due by month 6, remaining 35% split across months 7–24 as monthly invoiced amounts tied to usage floors
- Term discount: 18% off list for the 3yr commitment (applies when upfront >=25%)
- Milestone invoices (integration/enablement): Net 60 standard, but we can request a one‑time Net 90 exception for the first 3 milestones if finance requires it
- Escrow/assurance: optional holdback of 5% to be released on final acceptance in year 2 if CloudBridge requires added assurance

Questions for you:
1) Is the 25%/40%/35% split workable?
2) If finance insists on Net 90 for milestones, would CloudBridge accept the 5% holdback/escrow?
3) Any legal/Procurement clauses that will block a term discount tied to the partial prepay?

If this looks directionally good I’ll loop in Legal to prepare an amendment and circulate a DocuSign for the partial prepay SOW. Ben / Marissa — tagging you for pricing/legal input and to confirm the discount ladder.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Director, Strategic Sales — Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Payment cadence for multi-year commitment

Quick thoughts — I like the 25/40/35 split as a starting point. A couple of constraints from pricing:
- To preserve unit economics we need the term discount to be at least 15% for any partial prepay; 18% is acceptable but probably the max we should commit to without an escrow.
- If Finance pushes Net 90 on milestone invoices, we should require either (a) the 5% holdback you noted, or (b) acceleration language if CloudBridge misses ramp floors (2 consecutive months under floor = automatic catch‑up invoice).

If Legal is comfortable with the acceleration clause we can keep the 18% discount and grant the Net 90 request for the 3 initial milestones.

Ben
VP, Sales Operations
From: Paul Gray <paul.gray@cloudbridge.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudBridge Finance <acctops@cloudbridge.com>, Anna Li <anna.li@cloudbridge.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Payment cadence for multi-year commitment

Rachel / Ben — appreciate the flexibility. Finance confirmed they can do 25% upfront + 40% at month 6 with the remainder invoiced, but their controller insists on Net 90 for the first 6 months of milestone/integration invoices due to end‑of‑quarter constraints. They are open to a 5% holdback mechanism to be released upon final acceptance criteria. I attached the finance approval note (finance_approval_note.eml) showing their signoff on the split and the Net 90 ask.

One practical ask: can you include a short clause that ties release of holdback to objective acceptance criteria in the SOW? That will help speed approvals on our side.

— Paul
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Paul Gray <paul.gray@cloudbridge.com>, CloudBridge Finance <acctops@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T15:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Payment cadence for multi-year commitment

Paul — great, thanks for confirming. Next steps and agreed items below:

Agreed commercial summary:
- 3yr commitment, 25% upfront, 40% at month 6, remainder invoiced months 7–24
- 18% term discount applied to committed ARR once upfront paid
- Milestone & integration invoices: Net 90 for first 3 milestones, subject to 5% holdback released on objective acceptance criteria (SOW section 4.2)
- Acceleration: 2 consecutive months below usage floor triggers a catch‑up invoice (standard) — protects Redwood while preserving discount

I’ll have Legal add the acceptance criteria language to SOW v2 and circulate for signatures. DocuSign link will be sent once the amendment is ready: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?m=abc123

If everyone’s aligned I’ll route through HubSpot (deal RBW‑3241) and send final DocuSign by EOD Thursday.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this.

Rachel Kim
Director, Strategic Sales — Redwood Inference
https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567
